title: AppManifest
description: Protocol-level schema for app manifests. An app manifest is an EPR (content-addressed, stewarded, governed) that declares an app's content types, formats, renderers, relationships, and signals. The protocol validates the SHAPE of manifests (three-leg coupling, substrate signal mapping); apps validate their own vocabulary.

id.description: Content-addressed identifier for this manifest (CIDv1). Canonical EPR address.

name.description: Human-readable app name. Used in registry listings and governance references.

version.description: Semantic version of this manifest. Manifests are immutable once published; new versions create new EPRs.

description.description: Brief description of the app's purpose and domain.

rendering.description: Map of renderer name to RendererRegistration. Declares the rendering components this app provides for its content formats.

Vocabulary.title: Vocabulary
Vocabulary.description: The app's content vocabulary — the types, formats, relationships, and signals it declares. The protocol validates structural coupling; the app owns the semantic meaning of each entry.

contentTypes.description: Map of content type name to ContentTypeDeclaration. Each type must declare its three-leg coupling.

contentFormats.description: Map of format name to ContentFormatDeclaration. Declares how content is serialized and which renderer handles it.

relationships.description: Map of relationship name to RelationshipDeclaration. Declares the graph edges this app uses between content types.

signals.description: Map of signal name to SignalDeclaration. Declares the substrate signals this app emits, each mapped to an economic action.

ContentTypeDeclaration.title: ContentTypeDeclaration
ContentTypeDeclaration.description: Declaration of a content type within the app vocabulary. Every content type must declare its three-leg coupling — how knowledge, value, and governance attach to it.

description.description: Human-readable description of what this content type represents in the app's domain.

metadataSchema.description: JSON Schema defining the metadata shape for this content type. Enables typed metadata access and codegen. Can be inline or use $ref to a companion schema file. The protocol validates this is a valid schema; the app validates its content.

ThreeLegCoupling.title: ThreeLegCoupling
ThreeLegCoupling.description: The three-leg coupling contract for a content type. Every EPR carries lamad (knowledge) + shefa (value) + qahal (governance) dimensions. No value-blind content. No governance-free content.

KnowledgeLeg.title: KnowledgeLeg
KnowledgeLeg.description: Knowledge dimension of three-leg coupling. Declares how this content type relates to other content in the knowledge graph.

relationships.description: Map of relationship name to an array of target content type names. Declares which graph edges this content type participates in.

ValueLeg.title: ValueLeg
ValueLeg.description: Value dimension of three-leg coupling. Declares the economic flows triggered by interactions with this content type. Maps to REA (Resource-Event-Agent) economic actions.

onConsume.description: Economic flow triggered when a learner consumes this content (reads, watches, listens).

onComplete.description: Economic flow triggered when a learner completes this content (finishes assessment, reaches end).

onContribute.description: Economic flow triggered when a steward contributes this content (creates, curates, reviews).

ValueFlowEvent.title: ValueFlowEvent
ValueFlowEvent.description: A single economic flow event, mapped to a REA economic action. Declares what happens in the value network when this event fires.

resourceConformsTo.description: ResourceSpecification that the affected resource conforms to. References a protocol-level resource spec.

recognition.description: How this economic event is recognized in the value network (e.g. 'mastery-credit', 'stewardship-standing', 'contribution-record').

GovernanceLeg.title: GovernanceLeg
GovernanceLeg.description: Governance dimension of three-leg coupling. Declares how this content type is governed — its visibility reach, governance model, and the signals that can act on it.

defaultReach.description: Default reach level for new content of this type. Must be a valid reach value (private, self, intimate, trusted, familiar, community, public, commons).

minimumReach.description: Minimum reach level — content of this type cannot be more restrictive than this. Ensures governance-required visibility.

governanceModel.description: Governance model applied to this content type (e.g. 'steward-consent', 'community-vote', 'constitutional').

signalTypes.description: Signal types that can act on this content type. References signal names declared in vocabulary.signals.

ContentFormatDeclaration.title: ContentFormatDeclaration
ContentFormatDeclaration.description: Declaration of a content format — how content is serialized and rendered. Maps to a renderer and declares MIME types and file extensions.

renderer.description: Reference to a renderer name declared in the manifest's rendering section.

mimeTypes.description: MIME types associated with this format.

extensions.description: File extensions associated with this format (without leading dot).

aliases.description: Alternative names for this format, for backward compatibility or convenience.

bodySchema.description: JSON Schema defining the contentBody shape for this format. Enables typed body parsing and codegen. Used to generate body interfaces (e.g. EprCompositeBody for epr-composite format).

RelationshipDeclaration.title: RelationshipDeclaration
RelationshipDeclaration.description: Declaration of a relationship type — a directed edge in the content graph. Declares which content types can participate as source and target.

description.description: Human-readable description of what this relationship means.

sourceTypes.description: Content type names that can be the source (from) of this relationship.

targetTypes.description: Content type names that can be the target (to) of this relationship.

inverse.description: Name of the inverse relationship, if declared. E.g. 'contains' has inverse 'belongs_to'.

SignalDeclaration.title: SignalDeclaration
SignalDeclaration.description: Declaration of a signal type — an event emitted by app interactions that maps to a substrate signal and economic action. Signals are the bridge between user activity and the value/governance network.

description.description: Human-readable description of what this signal represents.

substrateSignal.description: The substrate-level signal category this maps to. Determines which resource dimension is affected.

economicAction.description: REA economic action triggered by this signal (e.g. 'use', 'consume', 'produce').

resourceType.description: ResourceSpecification this signal acts upon. References a protocol-level resource spec.

RendererRegistration.title: RendererRegistration
RendererRegistration.description: Registration of a rendering component that can display content in specific formats. Maps content formats to UI components.

component.description: Component identifier — web component tag name or framework component reference.

formats.description: Content format names this renderer can handle. References format names from vocabulary.contentFormats.

platform.description: Target platform for this renderer (e.g. 'web', 'tauri', 'universal'). Defaults to 'universal' if omitted.
